title: R1 RESEARCH: horizontal precedent among peer lineages - does an agent identity bind its own future, and do peer lineages bind each other
description: Research remainder 1 of 2 from the addendum's own agenda status (docs/serenissima-addendum-legal-theory.md section 8: "Item 1 (stare decisis mechanics): partially answered (section 5 vertical precedent); remaining: horizontal precedent among peer lineages"), scoped by coordinator decision A8. The addendum section 5 asserts as design input that "peer-level decisions are illustrative/persuasive, not binding" - your job is to TEST that against named primary sources, not to decorate it. Cover at minimum: whether a court binds its own future panels (UK House of Lords 1966 Practice Statement and its successor practice; US courts of appeals panel vs en banc and the law-of-the-circuit rule; Mexico's SCJN plenary vs salas and contradiccion de tesis), whether coordinate courts bind each other, and the mechanism that resolves a split between peers. Then map it: does an AGENT IDENTITY bind its own future sessions, and does one peer lineage bind another? Output docs/precedent-research/10-horizontal-peer-precedent.md. Same discipline as T-330..T-338: web research with named primary sources, every claim tagged, both mandatory sections, at least one finding that cuts against the commissioning brief. Zero build dependency by construction: this task must never wait on the build half.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY ONE FILE (create only this; touch no other file): docs/precedent-research/10-horizontal-peer-precedent.md. The parent directory already exists; use mkdir -p anyway (idempotent, race-safe: T-350 and T-351 run in parallel and share no file). Do NOT create or edit docs/precedent-research/README.md - that index is owned solely by the epic join T-362 (F1 single-owner rule). Do NOT edit 01..09, either v0 synthesis document, PRECEDENT.md, INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, or anything under .harness/.

WEB RESEARCH IS REQUIRED: at least 5 named sources, of which at least 3 are PRIMARY (a judgment with its case name and citation, a statute or code article, an official practice statement or court rule, or a named-author treatise / peer-reviewed article). Every source listed in a final Sources section with a retrievable identifier (case name plus citation, or URL plus retrieval date). A parametric-only claim with no locatable source is tagged SPECULATION, never ESTABLISHED.

EVERY substantive claim carries exactly one tag: ESTABLISHED (attributable to a named source in the Sources section), ANALOGY (a mapping from legal doctrine onto agent mechanics - this agent's inference, not the source's claim), or SPECULATION (neither). An untagged substantive claim is a defect and grounds for REJECT.

SUBSTANCE FLOOR, all four must be answered explicitly, each with sources: (a) does a court bind its own future panels, and by what mechanism does it release itself (UK 1966 Practice Statement; US law-of-the-circuit and en banc; SCJN plenary/salas and contradiccion de tesis); (b) do coordinate courts bind each other; (c) what mechanism adjudicates a split between peers, and who invokes it; (d) what happens to horizontal precedent when the deciding body is reconstituted.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Implications for the agent harness': map each finding onto the real substrate by name - blackboard task IDs, the three roles (thinker, worker, verifier) plus coordinator, the four authority tiers of D4 (1 operator, 2 constitutional, 3 verdicted, 4 single-agent), AND the two new v1 primitives: the graded force model of coordinator decision A2 (force as a spectrum raised by reiteration, decaying toward persuasive) and the typed operations of A4 (determination / reinterpretation declarative-corrective / valuation). For each finding state which schema field, CLI subcommand or protocol rule it demands, or state explicitly that it demands none.

MANDATORY SECTION titled exactly 'Extends, does not duplicate': for every doctrine that already has a partial answer in this repo, cite it by file and section and say whether the finding EXTENDS the existing record or would DUPLICATE it. The candidates you MUST address by name: docs/precedent-research/01-stare-decisis-mechanics.md's own verdict on horizontal precedent (it was already asked whether horizontal precedent is desirable here at all); SDR-04 in docs/precedent-research/synthesis-design-requirements.md, which already RULED that scope binds roles and substrate objects, never a reassignable agent identity string; the verifier-rotation rule F6 (ORCHESTRATION.md:119-126); and PR-004, the live seed record on verifier rotation. Rationale: a layer that re-does existing verification measurably regressed the corpus system (papers/agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:8 Table 3 RQ3a, p.9 'components interact non-additively').

MUST CONFRONT SDR-04 HEAD ON: SDR-04 already decided that scope binds the office, never the person, because agent identities are reassignable and reputation is per-identity (state.json agents.reputation). State whether horizontal precedent survives that rule at all - if an identity cannot be bound, what exactly is the 'lineage' that horizontal precedent would bind? Give a concrete answer (the role, the epic, the task chain, the registry subject key, or nothing), and name the mechanically observable object that carries it.

MUST TEST THE ADDENDUM, NOT FLATTER IT: the addendum section 5 states 'Peer-level decisions are illustrative/persuasive, not binding.' State whether your sources SUPPORT, CONTRADICT or QUALIFY that. If they contradict it, say so plainly with the citation. The addendum carries tier-1 authority as design input; testing it with sources is exactly the job, and a research document with zero friction against its commissioning brief is treated as unverified cheerleading.
MANDATORY: state at least one finding that CUTS AGAINST the addendum or against coordinator decisions A1-A8 where the sources support one. If the sources support none, say so explicitly and say why.
NO CODE, no edits under .harness/, no edits to PRECEDENT.md or INTERPRETIVE-CODE.md, no registry writes. Research tasks have no build dependencies and must create none.

Verification tier: DOC TIER per P-024 (proportional verification) - the verifier does a BRIEF replay (file exists at the exact path; every substantive claim tagged; Sources section present with the required counts; both mandatory sections present; spot-check that 2 named sources really exist), NOT a full adversarial replay. Deep evaluation happens at the synthesis gate T-352 and at the epic join T-362.

Hand off with `python3 .harness/bin/blackboard.py handoff --to-role verifier --agent <you>` (never self-mark done). The handoff note must name the 3 findings that most change schema v2, each carrying its tag.

notes.note: DECISION: plan - web research on (a) horizontal self-binding (UK Practice Statement successor practice, US law-of-circuit/en banc), (b) coordinate/peer courts NOT binding each other (sister circuits, coordinate district judges, SCJN Salas vs Pleno), (c) contradiccion de tesis / circuit-split-resolution mechanism, (d) reconstitution effect (Austin v Southwark-style succession). Map onto D4 tiers, A2 graded force, A4 typed ops, SDR-04, F6, PR-004. Test addendum sec 5 'peer-level decisions are illustrative/persuasive, not binding' against sources.

HANDOFF -> verifier: DECISION: Wrote docs/precedent-research/10-horizontal-peer-precedent.md (12 primary + 2 secondary sources, all substantive claims tagged, both mandatory sections present, substance floor a-d answered, addendum sec 5 tested). Replay: file exists at exact path; grep -c "ESTABLISHED\]\|ANALOGY\]\|SPECULATION\]" shows every substantive claim tagged; sections "Implications for the agent harness" and "Extends, does not duplicate" present verbatim-titled; Sources section lists 12 PRIMARY + 2 secondary, all with case name+citation or statute article or URL+retrieval date 2026-08-11. Spot-checkable sources: (1) Lord Reed of Allermuir, "Departing from Precedent: The Experience of the UK Supreme Court" (UKSC lecture, 20 Jan 2023) at https://supremecourt.uk/uploads/ukraine_departing_from_precedent_lord_reed_82d71af3e3.pdf -- verified by direct PDF fetch this session; (2) Contradiccion de Tesis 111/2013 (SCJN Pleno, resuelta 5 junio 2014, ponente Zaldivar) -- verified via scripta.up.edu.mx/handle/20.500.12552/6409 and SCJN's own engrose PDF.

3 findings that most change schema v2, each with its tag:
1. [ESTABLISHED+ANALOGY] Self-binding (does an identity bind its own future) and peer-binding (do peers bind each other) are TWO DIFFERENT DOCTRINES with two different mechanical carriers, not one: axis-one self-binding attaches to the ROLE (confirms SDR-04 unmodified -- nothing new demanded); axis-two peer-binding attaches to the PR record's `subject`+`authority_tier` pair, NOT the blackboard `epic` field and NOT agent identity -- epic-scoping would systematically under/over-detect real peer splits. This directly answers T-350's SDR-04 confrontation criterion with a concrete, two-track object (doc sec 6).
2. [ESTABLISHED] Addendum sec 5's "Peer-level decisions are illustrative/persuasive, not binding" is SUPPORTED for coordinate/sister bodies (US circuits/districts, UK first-instance, Mexico's two Salas -- none bind their coordinate) but is CONTRADICTED if extended to a body's own past self: UK Practice Statement/Reed lecture, US law-of-the-circuit, and Mexico's precedentes obligatorios all treat self-precedent as presumptively BINDING with narrow deliberate escape valves, never merely persuasive. This is the headline finding cutting against the addendum's silence on axis one (doc sec 5).
3. [ESTABLISHED+ANALOGY] Reconstitution of the deciding body's personnel releases nothing in every system with a source on point (UK: Reed's lecture -- "one of the things we inherited"; US: Miller v. Gammie) -- confirms D4/SDR-04's role-not-identity design was already correct, AND supplies new sourced evidence (UK's enlarged-panel practice, justified by name against "a differently constituted panel") for the already-standing SDR-07/01-F3 en-banc open question forwarded to T-348 -- sharpens but does not resolve it.

Additional schema-relevant demand (Implications F6, [ESTABLISHED+ANALOGY]): peer-split adjudication (CT 111/2013; US circuit-split resolution) is an A4 `determination` act (a forward-looking choice of which live reading controls), never `reinterpretation.corrective` -- PRECEDENT.md sec 12's adjudication-record fields should carry this A4 operation tag explicitly in schema v2.

No code touched, no other file edited, no .harness/ writes beyond the sanctioned blackboard.py/lock.py/session.py CLI calls. File is gitignored under docs/ by existing repo policy (A9.5) -- expected, not an error.
